"I played a lot of footy with them so it's going to be a little weird seeing them across the field," Manuleleua told NRL.com. "They've been the benchmark the last four or five years and we want to be the team that upsets them, just like we did with the Bunnies and Warriors.
"They pride themselves on a full 80-minute performance, they always back their fitness and are the team that tries to outlast others. It's worked for them, they keep grinding down teams until they cause an error and then they pounce.
"We need to make sure we play our style of footy, reduce our errors and if we go with them for the whole 80 minutes we can come away with the win."

Gagai out to write final chapter in 14-year odyssey
Newcastle veteran Dane Gagai has vowed to finish a journey he started back in 2012 by leading the Knights to their first grand final in 25 years.
The centre moved to the Hunter a fresh-faced 21-year-old back in 2012 and quickly developed into a key figure in the side's charge to the preliminary final the following season.
Gagai didn't realise it would be another 13 years before Newcastle would be back on this stage, the Queensland representative spending a stint at the Rabbitohs along the way.

Now back in a grand final qualifier, the centre has vowed to help the Knights upset Penrith in Sunday's blockbuster at Accor Stadium.
"To be able to get back to this position, not just for the club and us players but for the fans and the town is special," Gagai told NRL.com. "The support since I've been at this club is second to none.
"They were there in the dark times when we had three wooden spoons so it's nice to get back to this stage. We're not looking at stopping here.
"We've got a big challenge ahead of us with the Panthers and we're focusing on getting a job done so we can give the fans something to really be proud about."

'Thoughts of going home': The sliding doors moment behind Phillips' rise
Boom Panthers rookie Billy Phillips has revealed he nearly walked away from his rugby league dream as he battled home sickness during his first year in Sydney.
The 22-year-old has been dubbed the next Isaah Yeo but his NRL career was nearly over before it even began.
A Lake Cargelligo product who progressed through the Panthers junior pathway before moving to Sydney at the end of 2021 to chase his rugby league dream, Phillips couldn't crack the club's SG Ball side and featured in just one game in his first season.

Living more than six hours away from his friends and family, the young forward struggled with the adjustment and spent countless hours pondering a return home.
Now as he prepares to play his first preliminary final in Sunday's blockbuster against the Knights at Accor Stadium, Phillips has revealed how close he came to walking away.
"There were definitely thoughts of going back home," Phillips told NRL.com. "The move was hard, I was getting home sick and wasn't sure if this was for me.
"I had a great crew around me. The house parents that I moved in with and the boys I was with all pushed me to keep going. I got to train with the [Panthers development squad] Pearls and got to train with the Jersey Flegg boys the rest of the year.
"That was a good experience and got me ready for the next year. Then the next year I was off and racing."

The Newcastle Knights are determined to ride a wave of fan support all the way to the NRL grand final as excitement in the Hunter grows for Sunday's clash with the Panthers.
A convoy of Sid Foggs buses is set to descend on Accor Stadium on Sunday afternoon with the Knights desperate to continue their fairytale run through the finals series.
While the match is a Penrith home game, current sales data shows Knights fans have bought 65% of tickets.

More than a thousand fans descended on Knights HQ on Wednesday morning for an open training session, with supporters receiving a glimpse of their heroes up close.
"The town's buzzing and they deserve it," backrower Dylan Lucas said. "They've turned up for all those years when results haven't been so good so to now be able to repay that is special.
"You can't go and get a coffee without someone telling you how good the Knights are going and how happy they are that the Knights are going good. We've still got another job to do this weekend so we can't take those pats on the back, we've just got to keep working towards that goal."

It's been 25 years since Andrew Johns led the Knights to the 2001 premiership and 13 years since their last preliminary final.

Panthers coach Ivan Cleary insists star half and son Nathan is ready to go for the preliminary final against the Knights on Sunday afternoon.
But he also conceded there is a chance he might be playing with a foot fracture that could rule him out of the Rugby League World Cup .
Nathan Cleary during a Panthers training session this week. Wolter Peeters/SMH
Penrith went into full lockdown mode on Friday, pitching a series of black tarpaulins around their training facility to block out prying eyes, which only fuelled concerns of his fitness .
But speaking to media on Saturday morning, Cleary senior said Nathan had benefited from the week off and was “good to go”.
Cleary suffered the injury in the win over the Roosters a fortnight ago, and while he finished the match, his post-kick reaction – hobbling, unable to rise onto his toes, running on his heels – raised alarms. His late field goal also wobbled unnaturally – a stark contrast to his usual textbook strike.
Jack Cole has been named to partner Cleary in the halves, with Jack Cogger on the extended bench. The coach ruled out the suggestion his son could come off the bench, but switching Cogger and Cole remains a possibility.

items.title: Isaah Yeo makes decision on long-term future
items.snippet: Penrith Panthers skipper Isaah Yeo is set to re-sign with the club on a long-term extension, to have him remain at the foot ...
items.body_excerpt:
Penrith Panthers skipper Isaah Yeo is set to re-sign with the club on a long-term extension, to have him remain at the foot of the mountains.
Plenty of speculation has been bubbling away during 2026 about the long-term future of a bunch of Panthers stars off contract at the end of next season, including Yeo.
Although News Corp is reporting Yeo has agreed to an extension with the club, which will see him skyrocket past 350 NRL games in Panthers colours.
His new deal is expected to see him add an extra four years at Penrith from 2026.
There are also negotiations still ongoing of what a post-retirement role at the Panthers looks like.
Yeo has remained one of the Panthers' elite players for a long amount of time, and established himself as the pioneer ball-playing lock in the increased pace era in the NRL .
He is so crucial to the side's success that Yeo is currently playing with a torn pec to give the side every chance of raising the trophy on October next weekend.
SYDNEY, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 09: Isaah Yeo of the Penrith Panthers poses during the 2024 NRL Telstra Premiership Finals Series Launch at Hickson Reserve on September 09, 2024 in Sydney, Australia. (Photo by Mark Metcalfe/Getty Images)
Yeo has also flexed his muscle in the representative space, earning captaincy duties for both NSW and Australia for his fearless leadership during the Panthers' dominant four-peat.
Meanwhile, it is understood contract talks with Nathan Cleary are also progressing in the right direction amid heavy speculation of an exit.
Cleary has been tight-lipped for quite some time on what his future looks like, but fresh reports indicate the Panthers remain in the hot seat to secure his services beyond 2027.
The maestro halfback is free to negotiate with rival clubs on November 1 this year for a 2028 contract, and will likely attract interest from more than three thirds of the entire competition given his stature in the game.
With younger brother Jett set to return to Australia to continue his NRL development, Cleary may have the opportunity to play alongside him at Panthers clubland, potentially playing a pivotal role on what his next contract is.
Penrith stars Mitch Kenny , Isaiah Papali'i , Thomas Jenkins , Paul Alamoti and Casey McLean have all committed long-term to the club as they face a fresh chapter under Peter Wallace beyond next season.
Ivan Cleary will step down as Panthers head coach after 2027, with long-term assistant Wallace ready to take charge.
Yeo and Cleary's re-signings would be a massive show of faith for rookie coach Wallace as he begins a new chapter in his coaching journey in 2028.
The club will farewell fan-favourite Brian To'o , who is PNG Chiefs bound at the end of next year, while also losing many star comrades over the years in their premiership dominance.
The Panthers will host the Newcastle Knights at Accor Stadium on Sunday afternoon to book the last place in the Grand Final against the Sydney Roosters the following week.
